Target audience: University students (Computer Science/AI focus)

Section: section_1 — The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Bookshelf

Lecture lines:
Transformers use two distinct memory systems.
Attention retrieves contextual information dynamically.
MLPs store permanent factual knowledge.
Think of MLPs as an internal encyclopedia.
The brain analogy explains deep storage.

Planned animations:
Create a metaphorical bookshelf (color #FFFFFF) containing labeled book objects.
Introduce a neural network brain (color #00FF00) as a separate entity.
Demonstrate the search process where the brain finds specific patterns.
Highlight key retrieval paths between brain and books.
Fade everything to focus on the interconnectedness.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: The Concept of Vector Keys

Lecture lines:
MLP layers function as pattern matchers.
Inputs act as keys to locked gates.
Matching keys reveal stored fact vectors.

Planned animations:
Define vector keys as unique coordinates in space (color #FF00FF).
Display 2D vector space grid showing scattered key points.
Show vector query as a directional arrow moving toward a key.

Section: section_3 — Deep Dive: Rank-One Model Composition

Lecture lines:
Weights represent sums of outer products.
Training updates these to encode associations.
This forms a grid of knowledge nodes.
We see specific nodes illuminate concepts.
Outer products build the internal map.

Planned animations:
Define rank-one matrix as outer product of two vectors (color #00FFFF).
Show visualization of vector u and v scaling the model output.
Use flashing to emphasize the interaction between u and v components.
Assemble the components into a singular matrix structure.
Label the resulting rank-one model with #FFFFFF text.

Section: section_4 — The Mechanism: Pattern Retrieval

Lecture lines:
Input vectors undergo matrix multiplications.
Activation gates filter detected patterns.
Facts project into prediction space.

Planned animations:
Demonstrate pattern retrieval as a match-score calculation.
Show the inner product result (scalar value) scaling the output.
Animate the weighted retrieval process using color #FFCC00.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Distributed Nature of Facts

Lecture lines:
Facts are distributed across multiple neurons.
Robustness emerges from collective neuron activity.
Individual neurons don't store single facts.

Planned animations:
Summarize the distributed knowledge across the rank-one layers.
Fade out specific points to show overall concept retention.
Finalize with a consolidated view of memory as model parameters.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Transformers use two distinct memory systems.",
            "Attention retrieves contextual information dynamically.",
            "MLPs store permanent factual knowledge.",
            "Think of MLPs as an internal encyclopedia.",
            "The brain analogy explains deep storage."

        self.setup_layout("The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Bookshelf", lecture_lines)
        
        bookshelf = VGroup(*[Square(color="#FFFFFF", side_length=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        bookshelf.arrange(RIGHT)
        
        brain = Circle(color="#00FF00", radius=0.4, fill_opacity=0.5)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.place_in_area(bookshelf, "B2", "B4")
        self.play(Create(bookshelf))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(brain, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(brain))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Distributed Nature of Facts", [
            "Facts are distributed across multiple neurons.", 
            "Robustness emerges from collective neuron activity.", 
            "Individual neurons don't store single facts."
        ])
        
        # Define Neurons
        neurons = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(9)])
        positions = ["B2", "B3", "B4", "C2", "C3", "C4", "D2", "D3", "D4"]
        for i, pos in enumerate(positions):
            self.place_at_grid(neurons[i], pos)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            *[n.animate.set_color(ORANGE) for n in neurons],
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Pulse neurons to show collective activity
        self.play(
            *[n.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE) for n in neurons],
            *[n.animate.scale(1/1.5).set_color(ORANGE) for n in neurons],
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(neurons),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)
